# Feature 1: comment editing

PUT /api/articles/:slug/comments/:id. Auth required. Body: {"comment":{"body":"..."}}. Success returns the comment in addComment's shape.

Rules (name: source):
- comment-edit-permission: only the author may edit. app/src/app/routes/article/article.service.ts, updateArticle.
- non-author-status: forbidden status. Same file, updateArticle. deleteComment answers not-found instead because its query filters by author. I followed updateArticle because its check is explicit.
- missing-comment-status: not-found status. Same file, deleteComment.
- edit-window: not in the repo. Assumed no time limit. Open question for the user.
- edited-mark: not in the repo. Assumed: set Comment.updatedAt on each edit. app/src/prisma/schema.prisma has no auto-update on it, so set it explicitly as updateArticle does. No new column, so no migration.
- error-body: app/src/app/models/http-exception.model.ts and app/src/main.ts. Validation errors use addComment's errors-by-field body.
- status-codes: article.service.ts (addComment, updateArticle, deleteComment) and main.ts (unauthenticated).
- migrations: app/README.md, app/package.json (prisma.schema), app/src/prisma/migrations/. Not needed unless a column is added.
- unit-tests: app/jest.config.ts (testMatch), app/project.json (test target), app/package.json (test script). Put tests in app/src/tests/services/ and use app/src/tests/prisma-mock.ts.

Builder: route in app/src/app/routes/article/article.controller.ts, logic in article.service.ts.

If you are running this project locally, create a `.env` file at the root for these variables. Your host provider should included a feature to set them there directly to avoid exposing them. Here are the required ones: ``` DATABASE_URL= JWT_SECRET= NODE_ENV=production ``` ### Generate your Prisma client Run the following command to generate the Prisma Client which will include types based on your database schema: ```shell npx prisma generate ``` ### Apply any SQL migration script Run the following command to create/update your database based on existing sql migration scripts: ```shell npx prisma migrate deploy ``` ### Run the project Run the following command to run the project: ```shell npx nx serve api ``` ### Seed the database The project includes a seed script to populate the database: ```shell npx prisma db seed ``` ## Deploy on a remote server Run the following command to: - install dependencies - apply any new migration sql scripts - run the server ```shell npm ci && npx prisma migrate deploy && node dist/api/main.js ``` ---SCHEMA datasource db { provider = "postgresql" url = env("DATABASE_URL") } generator client { provider = "prisma-client-js" previewFeatures = [] } model Article { id Int @id @default(autoincrement()) slug String @unique title String description String body String createdAt DateTime @default(now()) updatedAt DateTime @default(now()) tagList Tag[] author User @relation("UserArticles", fields: [authorId], onDelete: Cascade, references: [id]) authorId Int favoritedBy User[] @relation("UserFavorites") comments Comment[] } model Comment { id Int @id @default(autoincrement()) createdAt DateTime @default(now()) updatedAt DateTime @default(now()) body String article Article @relation(fields: [articleId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade) articleId Int author User @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade) authorId Int } model Tag { id Int @id @default(autoincrement()) name String @unique articles Article[] } model User { id Int @id @default(autoincrement()) email String @unique username String @unique password String image String? @default("https://api.realworld.io/images/smiley-cyrus.jpeg") bio String? articles Article[] @relation("UserArticles") favorites Article[] @relation("UserFavorites") followedBy User[] @relation("UserFollows") following User[] @relation("UserFollows") comments Comment[] demo Boolean @default(false) }

content.text:
The repository does not give an edit window, so I can't name a value for it. The code currently has no time limit, which matches the assumption in the spec, and I made no changes.

**Rule checked:** how long after creation a comment may still be edited.

**Value used:** none. The spec (`specs/feature-1-comment-editing.md`, line 9) lists this rule as "not in the repo. Assumed no time limit. Open question for the user."

**Where I looked:**
- `specs/feature-1-comment-editing.md`: only the open-question note above.
- `app/src/app/routes/article/article.service.ts` (`updateComment`): checks the body, the article and comment match, and the author. It has no time check.
- `app/src/prisma/schema.prisma`: `Comment` has `createdAt` and `updatedAt` only, with no edit deadline field.
- `app/README.md`: no edit or comment policy. It points to a `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` at the repo root, which is not in the working tree.
- Repo-wide search for window, minute, hour, day, expire, grace and similar terms: the only match was `expiresIn: '60d'` in `app/src/app/routes/auth/token.utils.ts`. That is the login token lifetime, not a comment rule.
- Git history: one commit (`7bc6f07 app baseline`), no other branches or stashes.

**Result:** No edit window is set anywhere in the repo, so I did not add a time check or change the tests. If the team has an edit window, it is defined outside this repository, and I need its value before the code or tests can enforce it. The spec's open question still stands.
